value.why: Offense and opponent pace combine to set plays.
Expected possessions are the base unit of scoring; drive count differs from plays due to turnovers, punts and clock-killing.
Pass rate drives clock usage and yards.
Offensive EPA per play, opponent-adjusted, anchors points per drive for each team.
Opponent defense efficiency suppresses points per drive and changes the pass/rush split of scoring.
Success rate captures consistency: sustained-drive teams run more plays per drive and burn clock, differing from explosive-dependent teams.
Explosive-play rates raise scoring variance and the fat right tail of the total distribution.
Red-zone TD versus FG conversion changes points per scoring opportunity by up to 4 points per trip and regresses to league mean.
Turnover rates change the number of drives and field position, so expected turnovers (not lucky realized ones) enter the total.
Starting field position from special teams and turnovers sets scoring probability per drive.
Kicker range and accuracy determine how many stalled drives convert to 3 points and the key-number structure of totals.
Starter versus backup QB shifts both team points and pace and is only resolved late; total must be a mixture.
OL availability changes efficiency.
Wind, precipitation, temperature.
Roofs and surfaces change the weather exposure and passing environment, systematically shifting totals.
Penalty-prone teams lose drive efficiency and extend game clock; adds a small, persistent adjustment.
Crew-level flag rates (holding, DPI) alter drive extensions and game length with a small but knowable effect.
Teams scoring above or below their drive-efficiency expectation regress; recent points should be discounted accordingly.
Total residual and key numbers.
Home/away scoring correlation for BTTS.
Sharp totals incorporate weather and lineup information; the Kalshi ladder should be compared to the de-vigged consensus.
Total ladder implied distribution.
Divisional familiarity may lower scoring relative to efficiency-based projections and is knowable from the schedule.
Volume and open interest weight how much the price reflects information versus stale quotes, and bound feasible size.
Executed trades show where liquidity actually transacted, informing realistic fills and whether price moves are informed flow.
Pressure shortens drives and lowers totals.
Soft shells concede completions and add scoring.
Run defence controls clock and drive length.
Turns two team paces into the number of snaps that the total actually counts.
Deep rungs are tail events; the existing key-number input does not define tails.
The existing weather input lists data fields but not the response function or the forecast-versus-actual issue.

Stage t6: points and probability added to a full-game total by overtime under each rule era, quantifying either reading of the silent contract text; the 2025+ both-possess increment is unverified beyond secondary reports.
Market-free expected total (sum of both team means) and its drivers; the source of the 'expected total' that tail and joint-distribution inputs condition on.

Implied team means from game spread/total.
The team's own opponent-adjusted offense determines its points per drive independent of the other side.
Opponent defense efficiency (pass vs rush).
Own plays and drives, which depend on both offense tempo and the opponent's clock-usage, set the possessions for team points.
Possessions allocated to team.
Team-specific red-zone TD conversion sets points per trip; shrunk to league average.
Own kicker accuracy and range add FG points when drives stall, and affect clusters at multiples of 3.
The team's starting QB status is the dominant driver of its own total and resolves late.
Own OL health shifts sack/pressure rates and run efficiency, affecting points per drive.
Absence of receivers and backs reduces the team's scoring ceiling.
Field position and opponent turnovers.
Weather effects scaled by style.
Lead/trail effect on the team's late scoring.
Team-score mass at multiples of 3/7.
Sportsbook team totals and implied splits from spread and total give the benchmark for team-total rungs.
Consistency with game total and spread.
Volume and open interest weight how much the price reflects information versus stale quotes, and bound feasible size.
Executed trades show where liquidity actually transacted, informing realistic fills and whether price moves are informed flow.
The opposing coverage shell sets this offence's passing efficiency.
Run defence caps the ground game.
Pressure against this offensive line cuts scoring.
Creates the discrete team-score distribution that the team total ladder needs and replaces a mean times variance approximation.
Alters the mean and variance of the points associated with the same drive state, and is a coaching feature absent from this archetype's inputs.
Directly adds a team-total source that the offence-only inputs omit and shifts the lower rungs through the chance of scoring without the offence.
Gives the possession count its two-sided structure, which the existing own-pace input lacks.
Gives the opponent-style matchup the team-total chain needs, while the single defensive EPA input hides the pass and run split.

Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s6) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.
Provides the integer pmf (OT-inclusive and regulation-only) from which every KXNFLTEAMTOTAL rung is read, without importing market lines.
Joint home/away score pmf from which the single-team pmf conditional on the game state (pace, weather, script) is read for KXNFLTEAMTOTAL.

Interaction with opponent pass defence and own EPA: a pass-heavy offence's points are hurt more by a strong pass defence and a run-heavy one's by run defence; pass rate over expected also sets the play mix feeding the drive-result lattice.

Position-agnostic count of invitees with a fast prior sets how many draws reach the tail of the fastest 40, longest broad jump and highest vertical; secondary because it aggregates the per-prospect prior.

A named prospect only wins the fastest-40 market (player or position), or sets a jump or rep mark, if he performs that drill at the Combine; opt-outs of fast or explosive prospects reshape each drill's argmax, and the two jumps are usually skipped or performed together.

College track times, verified sprint data, jump marks and size give each participant's expected 40 time and broad jump before he tests; the vertical and the bench press have their own priors (nfl.combine_vertical_jump_prior, nfl.combine_bench_press_pool_and_prior).
Best of typically two 40 attempts and multiple jumps raises each participant's result above his mean by a variance-dependent amount.
Yearly best 40, broad jump, vertical and bench-press reps, and the record for each, anchor the order-statistic tail of each drill, including the 148-inch broad-jump strike.
Electronic timing, start trigger, indoor track and unofficial-to-official revision define the recorded number that settles.
Reports that a prospect will not run, is injured, or will only test at his pro day update the participation hazard.
Projected top picks skip drills more often; board rank is a covariate for opt-out, not a predictor of speed.
Strike of 148 inches, Combine-only scope and the missing tie clause for the fastest 40 come from the contract text.
Broadcast unofficial 40 times are later revised to official times, which can reorder the top two sprinters.
Recorded official Combine result and its timestamp are needed to audit each settled market.
Drills run by position group on fixed days, so the market state jumps when the fastest groups test before close.
KXNFLCOMBINE-BENCH26 (Most Bench Press Reps) exists in the series; its pool and prior are lineman-driven and not covered by the speed/jump inputs.
KXNFLCOMBINE-VERT26 (Highest Vertical Jump) exists in the series and needs its own prior and its correlation with the broad-jump field already modelled.
Season thresholds settle YES once any game clears the rung, so the realised maximum to date and remaining games define the live state.
Per-game probability that the final margin exceeds 51.5 points is a deep tail of the margin distribution conditioned on mismatch.
Per-game probability that combined points exceed 109.5 is a far upper tail of the game-total distribution.
Weekly argmax of game totals across the slate, with shared weather correlation and payout splitting.
Separate offence and defence scoring rates give each team's point distribution for the weekly highest-scoring team.
The 225+ rushing-yard contract needs per player-game exceedance probability combining carry volume and long-run tail.
A 52-point margin needs the leading team to keep scoring after the game is decided; coach and backup-QB behaviour set that.
Number of games and teams on the weekly slate (byes, Week 18 full slate) sets the baseline argmax share.
Integer scores tie at the weekly maximum often enough that the 1/N dead-heat payout changes expected value.
Historical season maxima of margin, total and single-game rushing yards by era anchor the tail and the rung choice.
Market-free team ratings give the pairing mismatches that generate blowouts and the expected scoring for shootouts.
A team's rating error is shared across its remaining games, which correlates per-game tail events for season maxima.
Backup or rookie quarterbacks on bad teams create the deepest mismatches that produce 50-point margins.
Very high totals need both teams to score; the joint upper tail of the two scores, not the sum of marginals, sets P(total > 109.5).
Wind, cold and rain suppress totals outdoors, so the weekly highest-scoring game leans toward domes and calm venues.
Defensive and return touchdowns add points without offence and accelerate runaway margins.
Benchmark only: team rush attempts are conditioned on the closing spread; carry volume uses nfl.carries with a market-free margin.
Per-carry explosive probability of the rusher decides whether volume turns into 225 yards.
Leading teams feed the back late, so blowout scripts add carries for the 225-yard contract.
Weak run defences allowing explosive runs are where single-game rushing records happen.
Starters are pulled at large margins, capping both further margin growth and a starter's single-game yardage.
Late-season resting of starters creates mismatches and lowers the scoring of resting teams in the weekly argmax.
The current kickoff regime shifts field position and scoring rates, so era base rates must be adjusted for it.
Regular-season scope, over-rung strikes, overtime inclusion and dead-heat 1/N splitting are read from the contract text.
Official rushing-yard corrections after a game can move a 223-227 yard performance across the 225 rung.
Weekly argmax markets are partly settled by earlier kickoff windows, so the running in-week maximum and close time condition the remaining games.
Integer team-score key-number PMF drives the weekly team and game argmax and the tie mass at the top; rates alone do not give it.
Weekly market close time relative to the last window (timing only, no price) sets how much of the week is already realised.
P(tie after regulation) from the market-free margin distribution and OT points under the current rule add the overtime mass that KXNFLHIGHSCORE explicitly counts.
Lead-back carry share and lead/trail-conditioned team rush attempts give the 28+ carry upper tail a 225-yard game needs.
Covers every non-rushing KXNFLGAMESPECIALS rung (passing, receiving, receptions, TDs, sacks, tackles, INTs, D/ST TDs, 100/100 combo), which previously had no inputs in this record.
KXNFLGAMESPECIALS lists quarter rungs (QPY250, QRY150, QREY150) whose window and overtime exclusion differ from the full-game rungs.

Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s7) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.
Context for HIGHSCORE, which counts overtime: market-free OT probability and OT points by rule era (9-17 points possible under both-possess).

Stage s7 receiving legs (receiving yards 250-300, receptions 15-20, receiving and 100/100 rungs): the top-target receiver's target share and depth set the volume from which the player-stat extreme family draws its reception and yardage tails.
Red-zone conversion decides field goal versus touchdown.
Game script lattice sets pass volume and lead sizes.
Wind and cold depress passing and kicking.
Turns means into tail probabilities for the 'N+' strikes used in the per-game count series.
Splits the team sack count into three separately estimable factors and brings the opposing quarterback into a defensive count.
Coach aggression on fourth downs and two-point tries and tempo drive field-goal attempts and the conversion counts.
Go-for-it versus kick policy and two-point policy by state set attempts for field goals and for the 2-point and 4th-down conversion counts.
Go-for-it policy on 4th-and-goal decides two-point attempts and goal-line fourth-down tries counted by KXNFL4DCONV and KXNFL2PTCONV.
Overtime probability adds possessions to counts if overtime counts and adds a small tail mass to dispersion; tie-count use sits in the league tie archetype.
Offensive success rate links to yards per play for the team-yards series and to short-yardage conversion; no first-down series is live.
Safety frequency is a rare-event tail input to the dispersion stage; generic and demoted to context.
Pressure drives sack counts for the team and game sack series.
Starting quarterback status and sack avoidance change dropbacks and sacks for team sacks and game sacks.
In-game quarterback exit risk changes the opposing sack pool and the team's yards; staged in the sack stage.
Practice and designation vintages feed the starting-quarterback availability probability used by the sack stage.
Plays per game bound every count; the opponent's pace and ball control matter as much as own pace.
Expected drives set the opportunities for field goals and stalled drives.
Kicker range and accuracy by distance, altitude and wind decide field-goal counts for KXNFLFG.

Strike construction (N+ half-point floors), the 2-point-try sack exclusion in KXNFLTEAMSACK, the 48-hour postponement clause and the regular-season window come from the sampled rules text; overtime treatment, data source and both-team postponement are unstated in it.
